edits.target: - DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST: before answering, strike from your candidate every specific word or phrase the clue already states, and keep only the remaining head.
edits.content: - DELETE-CLUE-WORDS TEST (mandatory; name the struck words in your one reasoning line): before answering, strike from your candidate every specific word or phrase the clue already states, including ordinals and numbers ('the third leader to bear this title' -> 'Dalai Lama', not 'third Dalai Lama') and any first name, title or nickname the clue supplies ('the only president named Chester' -> 'Arthur', not 'Chester A. Arthur'; 'his name was Zeb, but others called him this' -> the alternate name only, not alternate + 'Zeb'). Keep only the remaining head. For 'called / known as / nicknamed this' clues, the answer is ONLY the alternate name or title, never the alternate plus the original name.

edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'Title / office / rank held by A, B & C' (people from different countries or eras) asks for the ONE shared title noun, not a listed person or a country. Use the title the passages pair with every name. 'In this book / play / film / opera' plus a character or plot detail asks for the WORK's standard title, not the character, the author or the scene. Choose the title the passages repeat beside the named character and plot detail.

edits.content: - POSSESSIVE OWNER: in 'X & Y are in this organization's Hall of Fame, founded in 1967', 'this country's capital', 'this company's founder', the slot is the OWNER (organization, country, company), not the possessed thing the clue already names. A candidate repeating 'Hall of Fame' is wrong. Pick the owner whose own facts match the clue's other details and give its short common name or acronym.
